question.prompt: The greatest prime number that is a divisor of \(16{,}384\) is \(2\) because \(16{,}384 = 2^{14}.\) What is the sum of the digits of the greatest prime number that is a divisor of \(16{,}383?\)

solutions.title: Factor a difference of squares
solutions.explanation:
The given power of \(2\) reveals that \(16{,}383\) is one less than a square, which makes it easy to factor:
\[
16{,}383=2^{14}-1=(2^7)^2-1^2.
\]
Using \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\), we obtain
\[
16{,}383=(128-1)(128+1)
=127\cdot129
=127\cdot3\cdot43.
\]
It remains to check that \(127\) is prime. A composite number has a prime divisor no larger than its square root, because the smaller factor in a factor pair cannot exceed the square root. Since \(11^2<127<12^2\), the only primes we need to test are \(2,3,5,7,11\).

The number \(127\) is odd, its digit sum is \(10\), and its last digit is neither \(0\) nor \(5\), so it is not divisible by \(2,3,5\). Also,
\[
127=7\cdot18+1=11\cdot11+6,
\]
so neither \(7\) nor \(11\) divides it. Therefore \(127\) is prime. All prime divisors of the other displayed factors are smaller than \(127\), so it is the greatest prime divisor.

Its digit sum is
\[
1+2+7=\boxed{10},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
